question: Official and recorded history of flooding, ice, heavy snow, heat and wind that B2 does not yet join, Montana 2020 to 2026: IEM warnings, NCEI Storm Events, IEM LSR, FEMA NFHL, NWS/USGS river gauges.
bottom_line: B2 reads only 11 of the 29 IEM products checked, and of those FL.W returns zero events because its zone path drops polygon rows. In Montana 2020-2026 the IEM archive holds about 2,500 distinct events for the requested products in the five-year window (begin 2021-10-19 to 2026-10-19), most of them winter (WW.Y 865 events in window), flood (FA.Y 548, FL.W 43, FA.W 37, FL.A 35, FL.Y 10) and snow squall (SQ.W 78). NCEI county-coded rows of flood (76), flash flood (60), heavy rain (144), tornado (17), funnel cloud (35), lightning (8) and debris flow (11), 351 rows in all with points in 2020-2026, are dropped by B2 today. IEM LSR pulls match B2's cache row for row. NWPS covers 278 Montana river gauges with crest history (388 crests dated 2020-2026 at 119 gauges). FEMA NFHL is queryable (28,426 Montana polygons), but showing flood zones needs the owner's and counsel's ruling first; FEMA and USGS terms pages could not be read in this session.

WI.Y, HW.W, WS.W, BZ.W, EC.W, WC.W, IS.W, DS.W: zone path as built (DS.W has 0 events in 2020-2026)

ncei_storm_events: Add county-coded rows with BEGIN_LAT for Flood, Flash Flood, Heavy Rain, Tornado, Funnel Cloud, Lightning, Debris Flow under the same 5-mile point rule B2 uses for hail (76, 60, 144, 17, 35, 8 and 11 rows, 2020-2026)
Keep zone-coded rows of any type by zone (already in B2): heavy snow, winter storm, winter weather, blizzard, ice storm, cold and wind chill, frost and freeze, heat, drought, fog, wildfire, high wind
Show the FLOOD_CAUSE value beside Flood and Flash Flood rows (values: Heavy Rain / Snow Melt, Heavy Rain, Ice Jam, Heavy Rain / Burn Area)
Correct the B2 brief: tornado and flash flood are not joined today, and in Montana 2020-2026 their NCEI rows are county-coded
iem_lsr: Keep all LSR types within 5 miles (B2 does), with a type-word map for the label changes (HEAVY RAIN and RAIN; HEAVY SNOW and SNOW; EXTR WIND CHILL and WIND CHILL; EXCESSIVE HEAT and EXTREME HEAT)
Do not show magnitudes for codes 5, 6, 7, I and J until the IEM unit for each code is confirmed (the value ranges suggest inches for code 5 and degrees F for 6, 7 and I; unverified)
Drop or repair the two shifted rows (2022-12, 2023-08) with a counted note, as B2's parser docstring describes
river_gauges_NWPS: New kind: Gauge crest. Use the 278 Montana gauges; show the nearest gauges within a distance (25 miles is a starting proposal, not checked for fit), the gauge name, the distance and the crests with dates and stages
Only a gauge's own NWS minor, moderate or major stage words may be used, and only where that gauge has the stage (102 gauges have a minor stage; 57 have all four)
Drop the 3 malformed crest years and count them; the historic and recent lists repeat the same entries, so count once
recommendation.fema_nfhl: Hold. Do not join or show FEMA flood zones (layer 28) until the owner and counsel rule: the lender rule in 42 U.S.C. 4012a ties the special flood hazard designation to flood insurance, and AGENTS rule 5 forbids insurance eligibility statements. If approved later: point-in-polygon on the cell centre; an empty result reads as no mapped polygon in this service, never as no flood hazard.

kinds_and_words.Official alert: An NWS watch, warning or advisory row (IEM). Name the product in words (for example Flood warning, Areal flood advisory, Winter weather advisory). Say it was the forecast warning at issue time, not what happened. Zone products: This product covered the whole zone, not this spot alone. Flood, heat and winter products carry no hail, wind or tornado tags; keep the NWS damage threat tag rule (D4) for the FF.W rows (2) and SQ.W rows (12) that carry a damage threat value.
kinds_and_words.Record: An NCEI Storm Events row (official record compiled after the event, with lag). Say NCEI's database runs to its newest event. County-coded rows name the county; the point is where NCEI places the event.
kinds_and_words.Report: An LSR row (a report sent to the NWS). Reports are not a complete record; no report is not no event. Quote the remark as written.
kinds_and_words.Gauge crest: A river crest at an NWPS gauge (observed stage). The gauge is at a stream, not at the address; show the distance and the gauge name.
kinds_and_words.Mapped flood zone (hold): FEMA NFHL polygon label. Hold until the owner and counsel rule (see fema_nfhl).

forbidden_or_careful_words_in_new_text: damage (only as a source type word such as NON-TSTM WND DMG, or inside a quoted remark or tag label)
insured, insurance, eligible, eligibility, covered (as in insured), safe, all clear, no flood, flood-free, not in a flood zone, no hail, no wind as a fact
join_rules: Polygon events (as B2's parse_ww_shapefile for SV, TO, FF): NEW polygons only; county twins (GTYPE C) and EXP rows skipped; the time window is POLY_BEG to POLY_END (UTC); a cell is covered when its centre lies inside the polygon (even-odd test); a NEW polygon with no outline is counted and shown as such, never as no warning

Zone events: group rows by zone, phenomenon, significance, event number, year (D30); begin is the earliest NEW or CON issue time, else the earliest utc_issue on the event's rows (D25); a CAN row gives the end (cancelled at); an UPG row ends the lower event (D31); events with no end read end not recorded
County events: the cell's county (Census county boundaries, public domain, to be checked) and the same event rules as zone events
NCEI points (county-coded or hail or wind): within 5 miles of the cell centre, trailing five years, same as B2 hail rows; zone-coded NCEI rows: by zone, as B2 does
LSR: within 5 miles, all types, type word from TYPETEXT lower-cased through the type-word map
River gauges: nearest gauges by distance from the cell centre; the crest date and stage from the gauge record; no inference about flooding at the address
